subject: Recap: Discovery + Competitive shootout scope — LumenCare
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Clarke <sarah.clarke@lumencare.com>, procurement@lumencare.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Discovery + Competitive shootout scope — LumenCare

Hi Sarah / LumenCare team,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from Redwood and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as we scope the competitive shootout you requested. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you described
- Unpredictable latency spikes on longer generations (p95 frequently >500ms for 512-token responses)
- High unit cost on your current TGI-hosted endpoints (esp. at high concurrency)
- Occasional OOMs and degraded throughput during large-batch nightly jobs
- Need for on-prem / VPC deployment option for PHI-containing workflows

Current stack (from your notes)
- Inference: TGI cloud endpoints (managed) + some vLLM experiments internal
- Serving surface: REST-ish microservice that fans out to the model endpoint and has a Redis-based prefix cache
- Client workload: mix of short interactive chat (<=128 tokens) and episodic long-gen (512–2048 tokens) for summarization and coding-assist

Success criteria you emphasised
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms for 512-token gen on interactive paths (or clear plan for graceful degradation)
- Cost: >=30% reduction in tokens-served unit cost vs current TGI baseline at production concurrency
- Reliability: no OOMs at your 99th percentile load patterns for 3 consecutive runs
- Quality: delta within +/-2% on your evaluation set (precision/recall/ROUGE-like metric)
- Security/compliance: private deployment in your VPC with KMS support for keys used in inference

Proposed shootout matrix (high-level)
- Models: Llama2-13B (8-bit q4 variants), Mistral 7B, open-quantized 70B, plus your internal vLLM setup and Redwood hosted variants
- Runtimes: Redwood inference runtime (dedicated + private), vLLM (your baseline), TGI cloud endpoints (baseline)
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), memory usage, cost per 1M tokens (estimated), quality scores on shared eval set, failure/OOM counts
- Test harness: 3-day full-run + 1-day smoke + reproducible scripts we’ll share in the benchmark_proposal.xlsx attachment

What we need from LumenCare to get started
1) A representative eval dataset (small sample first) — you mentioned S3 earlier; we’ll need read-only link and any secrets/credentials (we can provide a presigned URL workflow if preferred)
2) Confirmation of the p95/p99 targets above and any additional acceptance rules
3) Clarify whether the on-prem run must be air-gapped or VPC-only (affects instrumentation)
4) Signed NDA (received — thanks) and an SOW trigger or approval to run live smoke tests in your staging environment

Attachments: benchmark_proposal.xlsx (draft test plan), nda_signed.pdf (copy received)

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Nov 19: Redwood SE to kick off smoke runs once sample data is available (Monica)
- Nov 20–22: 3-day competitive shootout (parallel runs vs vLLM / TGI / Redwood)
- Nov 24: Share results + recommendations; follow-up call to review

Assigned on our side: Monica Patel (SE) will lead the benchmark runs; Jordan Blake (solutions) will help with integration and SRE coordination. I’ll coordinate deliverables and the timeline.

Thanks — please reply with dataset link and confirmation on the acceptance criteria above.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

--
Attachment: benchmark_proposal.xlsx (proposal matrix)
Attachment: nda_signed.pdf (received)

From: Sarah Clarke <sarah.clarke@lumencare.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumencare.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + Competitive shootout scope — LumenCare

Thanks Marcus — this looks right and aligns with internal notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- On-prem constraint: we need the option to run inside our VPC initially (no air-gap required yet). KMS integration is a hard requirement for any private deployment.
- Current baseline numbers: our internal measurements of TGI endpoints show p95 ~480–520ms at 512 tokens during peak (we'll share the detailed dashboards), monthly spend on TGI ~ $42k for inference.
- Dataset link: upload complete; here's a presigned S3 link to a 5k-sample set for the smoke run: s3://lumencare-datasets/test_prompts_v1.jsonl (read-only). We will follow up with a slightly larger production slice if needed.

Two asks: 1) can you include a short run that shows behavior at 2x concurrency than our current peak? We suspect the biggest wins will show up there. 2) Please confirm whether any of your proposed runs will require us to open firewall ports to external IPs — we prefer VPC peering or presigned uploads instead.

Appreciate the clear milestones — if you can confirm the smoke-run window tomorrow morning PST, I’ll ensure the sample data is accessible and loop in our infra lead.

Cheers,
Sarah Clarke
Director of AI Platforms | LumenCare
sarah.clarke@lumencare.com
+1 (206) 555-0119

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + Competitive shootout scope — LumenCare

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick confirmation and for the sample data link. A few technical notes from the SE side and a proposed measurement plan (high-level):

1) Test bed configurations
- Redwood private (VPC): 1x A100-80GB equiv nodes (for larger models) + 4x A10G-style nodes for smaller models; we’ll run identical model variants to your vLLM/TGI baselines.
- vLLM baseline: reproduce with your current config; request container image or runbook if available.
- TGI cloud: use your existing endpoint config as the baseline (we'll instrument client-side to measure true end-to-end).

2) Variables to sweep
- Sequence lengths: 128 / 512 / 1024 / 2048
- Concurrency: 1x peak, 2x peak (as requested), and 4x burst sim
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 for batchable paths
- Quantization: float16, 8-bit / q4-style variants where supported

3) Acceptance thresholds (we propose to start here; happy to adjust)
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms for 512 tokens (interactive path)
- Cost: >= 30% reduction vs measured TGI baseline at equivalent throughput
- Quality: <= 2% degradation on your eval metrics (we’ll use the sample set and your scoring script)
- Reliability: zero OOMs during 3 full-run iterations at 2x peak
4) Data & instrumentation
- We will use your S3 sample for deterministic quality checks and synthetic load for concurrency tests.
- Instrumentation: Prometheus-style metrics + token-level traces; for private runs we’ll provide a read-only collector container to avoid opening ports if you prefer.

5) Timeline proposal
- Thu Nov 19 AM PST: smoke tests (Monica) — confirm specific hour and we’ll be ready
- Nov 19–22: full shootout runs (three iterations across runtimes)
- Nov 24: results deck + recommendation

I’ve attached the draft benchmark_proposal.xlsx with test cases, scripts, and the scoring matrix. Jordan, can your SRE team confirm the VPC peering option and whether they need an IP allowlist?

Marcus — we’ll prepare the smoke-run scripts and verify the instrumentation path. Sarah — if you can share the TGI endpoint details or a runbook, we’ll reproduce it as closely as possible.

— Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

--
Attachment: benchmark_proposal.xlsx
